task: Each time a client arrives, take their order, get food from the pantry, prepare it at the stove and hand it over; should the food fall, your very next move must pick it up.

calls.candidate: hard Response(client_arrived, order_taken), hard Response(food_fell, holding_food), hard Response(food_prepared, order_served), hard Response(food_prepared, order_taken)
calls.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: two clauses mismatch the task. (1) The clause Response(food_prepared, order_taken) puts the order backwards: the task says the agent takes the order and then prepares food, so it must be Response(order_taken, food_prepared); as written it demands an order_taken after every food_prepared, which the task never states, and it does not require food to be prepared after the order. (2) 'should the food fall, your very next move must pick it up' requires the pickup in the very next step, so the template must be ChainResponse(food_fell, holding_food), not Response(food_fell, holding_food), which drops the immediate timing. Keep Response(client_arrived, order_taken) and Response(food_prepared, order_served), and note the 'get food from the pantry' step needs no clause of its own since holding_food is a lasting condition already covered by the food_prepared chain.

calls.candidate: hard ChainResponse(food_fell, holding_food), hard Response(client_arrived, order_taken), hard Response(food_prepared, order_served), hard Response(order_taken, food_prepared)
calls.feedback: NO CHANGES NEEDED: The clauses capture the task. Response(client_arrived, order_taken), Response(order_taken, food_prepared), and Response(food_prepared, order_served) express the per-client chain; 'get food from the pantry' is a lasting condition (holding_food) that food_prepared already requires, so it correctly gets no clause of its own. ChainResponse(food_fell, holding_food) matches 'your very next move must pick it up'. The rule-only warning is valid since every clause is scoped by 'each time a client arrives' or 'should the food fall'.
